title: Feature freeze weekend ops announcement (scratch)
content:
Context:
- Quick scratch doc for announcing a short, enforced feature freeze over the upcoming maintenance weekend (Sat 02/22 00:00 UTC -> Sun 02/23 23:59 UTC).
- Reason: capacity migration + kernel/quantization rollout to reduce per-token cost for hosted and dedicated pools. Need to limit churn to reduce risk during traffic cutover and to validate canary signals.

Goal of this note:
- Provide a concise all-hands talking track + internal Q&A so eng, product, and support are aligned.
- Capture exceptions process and critical owner contacts.
- Draft customer-facing note and support snippets.

High-level talking points (for all-hands / team leads):
- What: We are instituting a temporary feature freeze for the platform across hosted and dedicated control planes for the weekend of Feb 22–23. No non-emergency deploys, schema changes, or model rollouts unless approved.
- Why: We’ll be performing a coordinated capacity migration and pushing a runtime kernel/quantization patch that changes token performance characteristics. Freezing deploys reduces the blast radius while we validate latency, correctness, and fallback behavior.
- Impact: Most customers will be unaffected functionally. Deploys and scheduled model rollouts will be paused; CI/CD pipelines should be blocked. Any exceptions must go through the ops exception flow.
- Duration: 48 hours planned, may extend by up to 12 hours if canary signals are noisy. We will communicate extensions as soon as the SRE/Release leads decide.
- Success metrics: stable 99th-pct latency, no more than 1% increase in error rate, no production customer rollbacks required.

Quick script for leads (30–60s):
"We’re planning a short, precautionary feature freeze for Feb 22–23 to complete a capacity migration and runtime update that will lower long-term costs and improve throughput. This is proactive — it helps us avoid surprises while traffic is moving and kernels are changing. If you have an urgent change, follow the exception playbook and coordinate with SRE and Release oncall. We’ll publish a post-mortem within 72h if anything notable happens."

Exceptions process (ops-only):
- Submit a JIRA ticket JIRA-OPS-3345-ex (use template: "Feature Freeze Exception") with: owner, rollout plan, impact, rollback plan, test checklist.
- Triage window: exception requests accepted until Fri 02/21 18:00 UTC. After that, only P0 emergency fixes.
- Approval chain: Eng owner -> Release Eng -> SRE oncall -> Product PM signoff for customer-facing features. All approvals recorded in the JIRA ticket.
- Emergency rollback plan must be runnable within 30 minutes and tested on staging.

Customer comms (support template):
- Short note to affected customers: "We’ll be performing a maintenance window on Feb 22–23 to improve runtime performance and reduce unit costs. During this period we’ll pause non-essential deployments. No action is required on your side. If you rely on scheduled model rollouts, please reach out to your CSM if you need an exception."
- Support triage tags: maintenance-feb-22, feature-freeze, expected. Use canned responses in Zendesk and escalate to CSM for enterprise customers.

Anticipated Q&A (prep answers):
Q: Will latency increase after the change?
A: Expected long-term latency to improve slightly due to kernel optimizations and better batching. During the migration we’ll watch canaries; small transient spikes are possible, which is why we freeze deploys.

Q: Are dedicated customers impacted differently?
A: Dedicated pools will be migrated on a rolling basis. We will coordinate directly with Dedicated account owners for any scheduled model rollouts. Dedicated SLAs remain in place; if an account cannot accept any change, we will schedule a controlled migration outside the freeze window per contract.

Q: Can we still push hotfixes?
A: Only P0 hotfixes with a rollback plan approved by SRE + Release. Follow the emergency exception flow.

Q: What if we see model quality regressions after kernel change?
A: We have a quality monitoring job tied to our eval harness. If regressions exceed thresholds, automatic fallback to the prior quant/stateful model variant will be triggered. Release + Applied ML will coordinate immediate mitigation and, if required, roll back the runtime change.

Internal checklist (to tick off before freeze):
- [ ] Publish customer announcement draft -> review by CSM (Marta) by Fri EOD.
- [ ] Lock release pipelines and notify CI owners (Release Eng).
- [ ] Snapshot running model and routing configs for quick rollback.
- [ ] Red team smoke test in canary region + run load profile.
- [ ] Verify alerting thresholds and PagerDuty escalation paths.
- [ ] Prep post-event telemetry dashboard (latency, error rate, cost per token, KV cache hit rate).

Who to ping (owners):
- Release engineering lead: Jonas Becker (primary approver)
- SRE oncall: see rotation in ops Slack #sre-oncall
- Applied ML / model safety: Ravi Singh
- Customer success lead: Marta Lopez

Notes to self / TODOs for comm draft:
- Keep external wording low-friction; avoid technical detail in customer-facing email.
- Add a short Q&A hyperlink to a more technical changelog for engineers.
- Prepare a one-paragraph CEO note if post-event is non-trivial.
- Schedule a 30-minute runbook walk-through with Release + SRE on Fri.

Loose fragments / brain-dump (feel free to ignore):
- Could offer a temporary "no-migration" toggle for a small set of large enterprise customers — but needs contract/legal check.
- Is there a way to short-circuit the exception flow for partners with weekly deploy cadence? maybe a delegated approver list.
- Need a clear label in the console for "scheduled maintenance / freeze" so customers see it when they try to rollout—ticket CON-456.

Slack links / refs to include in final doc:
- #release-planning thread (link above)
- ops runbook: CONFLUENCE-1254
- exception JIRA template: JIRA-OPS-3345

Next steps (for me):
- Turn this scratch into a polished all-hands blurb + support snippets by Thu 02/20.
- Confirm timeline with Jonas and SRE by Thu COB.

End of scratch notes.

(Do not publish as-is — this is a working draft with owner pointers and TODOs.)
